subject: Critical kernel compatibility advisory — immediate action required
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Brightlytics Ops <ops@brightlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Oct 2029 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Critical kernel compatibility advisory — immediate action required

Hi Emily / Brightlytics team,

We're reaching out with an unscheduled advisory that may affect inference stability for long-sequence, large-batch workloads on Ampere 80GB-class GPUs. During our overnight telemetry sweep we observed a low-frequency memory-coherence issue triggered by a recent kernel ABI change from upstream that interacts poorly with our continuous-batching path. The issue can manifest as intermittent OOMs or silent token truncation under heavy KV cache pressure.

What we're doing now:
- Preparing a targeted hotfix (attached patch) to guard the kernel interaction and tighten memory fences in the runtime.
- Scheduling a short, out-of-band canary rollout to a small subset of capacity in us-west-2 within the next 60–90 minutes.
- Keeping your routes pinned to the current model variant unless you opt into the canary.

Customer ask / recommended immediate mitigations:
- If you have scheduled long-sequence batch jobs in the next 2 hours, please either reduce batch_size by ~50% or set max_seq to your typical 1.5x working set for the window.
- If you want us to run the canary against a subset of your traffic, reply with the route IDs and we will coordinate.

Attachments: kernel-compat-hotfix.patch (diff), brightlytics-canary-checklist.md (run steps).

We understand the disruption risk of an unscheduled change — the canary is designed to validate both performance and token integrity before a wider rollout. We'll post progress to the incident link below and update your support ticket RI-98762.

Status: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/INC-20291014-01
Support ticket: https://support.redwoodinference.com/tickets/RI-98762

I'll follow up within 30 minutes with the canary window. If you prefer we pause all non-critical jobs across your routes, tell us and we'll enforce a temporary throttle.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---
(Attachment: kernel-compat-hotfix.patch; brief diff, applies to runtime/kernel-binding layer)

From: Emily Torres <etorres@brightlytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Brightlytics Ops <ops@brightlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Oct 2029 09:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Critical kernel compatibility advisory — immediate action required

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the heads up. A couple quick questions before we decide on canary opt-in:

1) Do you have an estimate for end-user impact (error rate / latency spike) for the canary vs no-change? Our SLAs are tight during our morning peak.
2) If we opt in, can the canary be limited to the non-production routes (we have route IDs: brightlytics-prod-read and brightlytics-analytics)?
3) If the hotfix fails validation, what's the rollback plan and expected time to revert?

We will pause scheduled batch jobs for the next hour while you confirm. If you can confirm minimal impact on p50/p95 latency, we can consider a limited canary on brightlytics-analytics only.

On Mon, Oct 14, 2029 at 08:12 Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> We're reaching out with an unscheduled advisory that may affect inference stability for long-sequence, large-batch workloads on Ampere 80GB-class GPUs. ...

— Emily Torres
VP, Platform Engineering
Brightlytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Torres <etorres@brightlytics.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Oct 2029 09:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Critical kernel compatibility advisory — immediate action required

Emily — quick technical note and proposed plan.

TL;DR: Canary is low-risk if limited to a single dedicated instance pool and we will not alter route DNS — we'll only pin traffic at the load balancer level for the test. Rollback is immediate: we maintain old kernel-binding and can switch back within ~3 minutes.

Details:
- Impact estimate: during our internal stress test the issue caused ~0.2–0.5% silent truncation in pathological workloads and occasional OOMs under sustained 2k token sequences with batch_size >= 32. Typical production traffic with shorter sequences saw negligible effect. Expected latency change from the hotfix is +3–7ms at p95 on heavy sequences.
- Canary scope: single canary pool in us-west-2 (3 GPU instances) pinned to your 'brightlytics-analytics' route if you approve. No DNS change; traffic sampling only.
- Validation checklist (see attached brightlytics-canary-checklist.md): token-integrity checksum on sample prompts, end-to-end smoke-test, KV cache pressure test, end-user latency sample. We will collect logs and attach canary-run-logs.txt.
- Rollback: if checksum divergence or error rate >0.5% we abort and revert the binding; revert path is automated and tested — revert window ~= 3 minutes, with additional validation for a further 10 minutes.

If you authorize, we'll start the canary at 09:40 UTC and report a pass/fail by 10:10 UTC. If you'd rather we only run a dry-run (no live traffic) we can do that at 09:40 as well and provide results by 09:55.

— Ben Carter
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: canary-run-logs.txt; kernel-compat-hotfix.patch)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Torres <etorres@brightlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Oct 2029 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Critical kernel compatibility advisory — immediate action required

Emily — thanks for the quick reply and for pausing your scheduled jobs.

We'll proceed with a limited live canary on brightlytics-analytics as Ben outlined. Start time 09:40 UTC already slipped due to final signing; new window will be 14:20–14:40 UTC (us-west-2). We apologize for the condensed notice.

What you'll see from us:
- Live canary telemetry to the status page and ticket RI-98762.
- Token-integrity checks and sampled p50/p95 latency graphs.
- Immediate rollback if any of the canary-check thresholds are hit (we will call out transparency metrics in the ticket).

Postmortem: independent of the canary outcome we'll schedule a 30‑minute postmortem with your team and engineering on Wednesday 2029-10-16 to go over root cause, timeline, and any compensating controls. I'll send a calendar invite after the canary completes.

Thanks for the quick coordination — we know these windows are disruptive and appreciate the partnership.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

(Links: incident page, support ticket; Attachments re-sent: kernel-compat-hotfix.patch, brightlytics-canary-checklist.md)
